key_points.point: CONNECTING THE DOTS… 5 5.1 Of Questions and Statements Your teacher tells you that they are meeting two of their childhood friends this evening.
One is 5 feet tall and the other is 6 feet tall.
What is your guess as to each friend’s gender based on this information?
You might have guessed that the 5-foot-tall person is a woman and the 6-foot-tall person is a man.
But experience tells us that 5-foot-tall men and 6-foot-tall women are rare.
We have seen that, more often, men are taller than women.
The above is a simple example of statistical thinking.
We regularly come across statements like — Jemimah’s batting has been very consistent over the past year.
